{
  "research_question": "How does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, or Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Success rate is lowest in the Sham group (0.273) and higher in all stimulation groups (0.67-0.78), indicating stimulation generally facilitates finding the target.",
    "Time-to-Target is longest in the Sham group (4.68s), while Combined (2.56s) and ICMS Only (3.05s) groups are faster than Sham, though Dim Visual Only is the slowest stimulated group (3.14s).",
    "Path Efficiency is highest in Bright Visual Only (0.504) and Combined (0.502), while it drops significantly in Sham (0.308) and is lower in ICMS Only (0.432) and Dim Visual Only (0.434).",
    "Average Speed is highest in the Combined group (12.83) and lowest in Sham (10.74); stimulation does not drastically reduce speed, but Bright Visual Only is slightly faster than Dim Visual Only.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is highest in the Combined group (0.399) and lowest in the Sham group (0.236), a stark contrast to Path Efficiency where Combined also performs well."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success: Sham (0.273) vs. Bright Visual Only (0.785) show the largest gap (0.512).",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.682) vs. Combined (2.562) show the largest improvement (2.120s).",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) vs. Bright Visual Only (0.504) show the largest gap (0.196).",
    "Average Speed: Combined (12.833) vs. Sham (10.737) shows the largest difference (2.096).",
    "AD: Combined (0.399) vs. Sham (0.236) shows the largest disparity (0.163), suggesting Combined stimulation increases path meandering compared to absence of stimulation."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Stimulation paradigms generally improve navigation metrics compared to Sham, with the highest Success rates and fastest Time-to-Target observed in the Combined group. However, the Combined group exhibits the highest Angular Dispersion, implying that while it results in faster target acquisition, the path may be less direct or more erratic. The ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only paradigms show intermediate performance, often lagging behind the Combined and Bright Visual Only groups in efficiency and success.",
  "limitations": [
    "Arsenal Data contains only Population Means and Standard Deviations; individual subject variability and p-values for group comparisons are not provided, precluding hypothesis testing.",
    "The large disparity in sample sizes between groups (Combined n=48846 vs. Sham n=3505) could influence the magnitude of calculated means if data is not perfectly balanced or if the metric distributions are skewed by outliers.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) interpretation relies on the supposition that higher values indicate less direct paths; without the distribution shape, the practical implication of a 0.16 difference is inferred as increased meandering but could also indicate exploration behavior."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Calculate effect sizes (e.g., Cohen's d) between the Sham group and each stimulated group for all five variables to quantify the magnitude of differences, given the available summary statistics."
}
